pull.title: KAFKA-21230: Build RocksDB WriteBatch at commit
pull.body:
`RocksDBTransactionBuffer` writes every staged write twice: to `pendingWrites` on the heap, which serves reads, and to a native RocksDB `WriteBatch`. The `WriteBatch` holds native memory for the whole transaction, and the buffer changes it while it holds the write lock.

The buffer now stages writes on the heap only. Writes to other column families and range deletes also stay on the heap until the commit. At commit, `prepareFlush()` builds the `WriteBatch` from the staged state outside the write lock, and `flushToBase()` writes it to RocksDB under the write lock. A JMH model of the two designs measured writes 2 to 7 times faster, and commits 8 to 12 times faster when the transaction overwrites keys. A commit with no overwrites and 1000-byte values is up to 28% slower.

Because no buffer writes to a backend at stage time now, the `stageToBackend` hook of `AbstractTransactionBuffer` has no function. This change removes it and all of its implementations.

The uncommitted-bytes estimate also counted a key once for each write in a transaction, so a key written many times could cause an early commit with little staged data. `AbstractTransactionBuffer.stage` now subtracts the size of the previous entry for the key before it adds the new entry. `RocksDBTransactionBuffer` uses this shared accounting for all of its staged data.

`statestore.uncommitted.max.bytes` now counts each staged write once. Before, it counted the heap copy and the `WriteBatch` copy. The commit still needs a native `WriteBatch`, but only for one store at a time, because stores commit one after the other. The extra memory at commit is therefore at most the uncommitted bytes of the largest store. A thread now commits early when its uncommitted bytes plus the uncommitted bytes of its largest store exceed its share of the limit. The global thread uses the same check. The limit is thus again a bound on the memory at commit.

The check uses the largest value of `StateStore.approximateNumUncommittedBytes()`, so it needs no change to a public interface. In-memory stores need no extra memory at commit, so applications with only in-memory stores commit early after less data than in 4.4. Applications with more than one transactional RocksDB store can buffer more data before an early commit. The 4.5.0 upgrade guide and the documentation of the config record this. The default stays at 64 MB.

commit.message:
KAFKA-21230: Fix byte count for overwritten keys in transaction buffer

The uncommitted-bytes estimate of a transaction buffer is too high when
the same key is written more than once in one transaction. The estimate
can then reach the pause threshold when the real amount of staged data
is smaller.

The buffer added the key size and value size on each write. It did not
remove the size of the value that the write replaced. A key written
many times was counted many times.

AbstractTransactionBuffer.stage now subtracts the size of the previous
entry for the key before it adds the new one. RocksDBTransactionBuffer
had its own copy of the byte counting. It now calls the shared
implementation for its default column family, and its stageToBackend
writes to the write batch directly. This keeps the counting in one
place and prevents a double count from the shared path.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
KAFKA-21230: Remove the stageToBackend hook from transaction buffers

The RocksDB transaction buffer now builds its WriteBatch at commit
time, from the staged state. Because of this, no buffer needs to be
told about each write when it is staged. Every implementation of
stageToBackend was a no-op.

Remove the abstract method, its call in the put path, and all of its
implementations. Update the test buffer to flush from the pending
writes map instead of keeping its own copy of the pending batch.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
KAFKA-21230: Bound commit memory in the uncommitted-bytes limit

A thread pauses processing and commits when its uncommitted bytes pass
its share of statestore.uncommitted.max.bytes. A commit can itself need
extra memory. The thread can therefore go over the limit while it
commits.

Stores commit one at a time. During the commit of one store, the extra
memory needed is up to the size of that store's uncommitted data. The
largest store gives the worst case.

Add maxStoreUncommittedBytes to ProcessorStateManager, Task and
TaskManager. It returns the largest uncommitted byte count of any one
store. StreamThread now adds this value to the total uncommitted bytes
before it compares the sum with the limit.

Apply the same check to the global state thread. Add
maxStoreUncommittedBytes to GlobalStateManager and
GlobalStateMaintainer, and make GlobalStreamThread compare the total
plus the largest store's bytes with its limit.

Both threads now commit earlier, so the commit stays inside the limit.
Update the statestore.uncommitted.max.bytes documentation and the 4.5.0
upgrade guide to describe the new check and how it changes the point of
an early commit compared with 4.4.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

files.patch:
@@ -71,6 +71,8 @@ Processors returning the same `StoreBuilder` instance from `ConnectedStoreProvid
 
 Upgraded RocksDB dependency to version 10.10.1(from 10.1.3). RocksDB deleted `max_write_buffer_number_to_maintain` from its `ColumnFamilyOptions` in version 10.5.0. To preserve compatibility, Kafka Streams' `Options#setMaxWriteBufferNumberToMaintain` and `Options#maxWriteBufferNumberToMaintain` are now deprecated no-ops: the setter has no effect, and the getter always returns `0` regardless of what was previously configured. This change is primarily relevant to users implementing custom RocksDB configurations via `rocksdb.config.setter`. Users relying on `max_write_buffer_number_to_maintain` should remove that configuration, since it no longer has any effect. Consult the [RocksDB changelog](https://github.com/facebook/rocksdb/blob/main/HISTORY.md) between 10.1.3 and 10.10.1 for other changes.
 
+Transactional RocksDB stores now build their write batch at commit, not on each write. The commit of a store needs extra memory up to the size of the uncommitted data of that store. To stay within `statestore.uncommitted.max.bytes`, a thread now commits early when its uncommitted bytes plus the uncommitted bytes of its largest store exceed its share of the limit. Applications with more than one transactional RocksDB store can therefore buffer more data before an early commit than in 4.4. Applications with only in-memory stores commit early after less data than in 4.4.
+
 ## Streams API changes in 4.4.0
 
 Kafka Streams does not support the asynchronous bootstrap DNS resolution mode introduced by [KIP-909](https://cwiki.apache.org/confluence/x/MJtbDg) yet. For every client it creates internally, `bootstrap.resolve.timeout.ms` is forced to `0`, and a user-supplied positive value, through any prefix form, is ignored with a warning.
